html:
Reference city: nine regions

The user's numbered image is interpreted as a three-by-three grid. The active target is the user's replacement /Game/Levels/NewMap.NewMap in ForgeMCPDev. The deleted troubleshooting maps are preserved only as recovery copies and are not restored by this workflow.

Geometry and ownership

Region District
1 Northwest islands and park
2 Northern districts
3 Northeast district
4 Western mainland
5 Central island and tower district
6 Eastern crossings
7 Southwest interchange
8 Southern street grid
9 Southeast waterfront

The current source contains 7,200 building masses and 80 spatial chunks, with a 512-metre target chunk size. Region boundaries follow the image's numbered grid. Land triangles are clipped to chunk bounds. Buildings are assigned once by their centres; their footprints can extend slightly beyond a chunk boundary. Roads are segmented and major road corridors exclude building footprints. Bridges are split between chunks rather than held by one city-wide heavy actor.

Scale is provisionally three metres per image pixel: the full area is 3.762 km square and each numbered region is 1.254 km square. This is a deterministic manual interpretation of the drawing, not a surveyed 1:1 reconstruction. Building forms, street grids, shorelines and bridge details require further reference matching. The scene is a blockout, not completed photorealistic content or native PCG/spline graph exposure.

Streaming design

Each numbered region has an editor-only native LocationVolume controller with a BoxComponent describing its bounds. Unreal's LocationVolume loader uses the actor's component bounds. Native Load/Unload controls are intended for selecting regions in the World Partition editor. Heavy static-mesh actors use bIsSpatiallyLoaded=true; a single inexpensive water plane uses false.

World Partition runtime streaming is controlled by streaming sources and runtime grid settings. A numbered editor loading volume does not itself implement a runtime region-toggle API. Interactive Load/Unload, persisted reload behavior, runtime streaming and memory/frame-time measurements are separate acceptance checks. Region ownership alone cannot guarantee that the engine will not crash.

Source and recovery

The final version is Saved/ReferenceCityRegions_v2/Chunks512_Final/:

  • manifest.json: coordinates, region ownership and build order.
  • ReferenceCityRegions_v2.blend: export-space source with local chunk origins.
  • ReferenceCityRegions_v2_Layout.blend: separate assembled review copy.
  • Nine_Region_City_Overview.png: rendered review of the assembled source.
  • geometry_report.json: per-chunk geometry and material counts.
  • *_transfer_result.json: individual transfer receipts.
  • asset_preparation_progress.json: completed asset preparation.

Earlier city versions remain preserved in their original directories. Imported meshes are placed under /Game/ReferenceCityRegions_v2/R01 through R09; controllers and water use separate Controllers and Background folders.

prepare_city_region_assets.py prepares and saves assets without level placement. It resumes only completed receipts and stops on partial or uncertain operations. Create pause_asset_preparation in its source directory to stop after the current atomic import finishes.

install_city_regions.py verifies the explicit live project, level and PIE state, then uses typed native previews and applies. It checkpoints each placement and reloads only after a verified checkpoint. A failed checkpoint stops installation without discarding the active level. --reload-once retains per-placement checkpoints but defers the level-open step until all nine regions have been saved. This avoids interrupting a paused-editor construction pass with repeated world reloads.

Verified and pending evidence

The final Blender source was assembled, saved separately and rendered. Regional geometry and level-workflow tests passed: 33 tests. The full Python suite then passed all 380 tests. Ruff passed for the five city scripts. The first test command used system Python, which lacks pytest and ruff; the successful validation used the repository's .venv interpreter.

Unreal mesh import and material saves are recorded individually. Native import currently triggers repeated static-mesh/distance-field work while material slots are assigned, which can delay Editor interaction. No global renderer setting has been disabled to conceal this cost.

Current-level checkpoint attempts previously failed the native stale-state guard. Two actor-property samples showed a changing Ultra Dynamic Weather Current Lightning Angle; the sampled sky actor values remained unchanged. The user disabled viewport Realtime, after which the guarded checkpoint succeeded with native backups and independent package-file verification. The guard remains enabled. Evidence: realtime_off_checkpoint.json, operation 1e504ee84c041ef6e066ff8b0fcf5449. This establishes a successful checkpoint under the paused editor condition, without proving that this single weather field was the only changing value. Complete region placement, saved/reloaded controls, interactive loading, PIE and performance remain separate checks.

All 81 mesh assets (80 chunks and one water surface) have completed saved transfer receipts. Nine controller placements were checkpointed during the first placement pass. Regions 5, 4, 6 and 2 were placed, checkpointed and inspected after the native level-open request. Their actors remained loaded after those requests, so these observations do not prove regional unloading. The pass stopped on another stale checkpoint during region 8; the installer retained the active level. Remaining placements and final persistence verification are still in progress.
